description: Hi everyone! I’m Ahmad Hassan, a Software Engineer / Computer Science Student  based in FSD, Pakistan. I am absolutely fascinated by space exploration, and for this year’s NASA Space Apps Challenge, I am building a "Lunar Landing Site Navigator" an intuitive, interactive Go/No-Go risk dashboard for Artemis mission planners to evaluate lunar south-pole landing sites based on solar power availability and direct-to-Earth communication windows.
summary:
LUNA-GUARD is a NASA Space Apps lunar mission intelligence platform combining live NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data with Random Forest ML terrain estimates.

The dashboard includes five core modules:

Overview: Central command tracking real-time telemetry, a 71/100 CAUTION readiness score, and power margins.

Mission planning: Simulation workspace for configuring landing sites, launch dates, durations, and power loads.

Sites & terrain: 3D lunar South Pole globe and ranking table comparing landing zones (e.g., Malapert Massif at 97/100).

Power: Hour-by-hour solar generation, battery state-of-charge, and multi-cycle energy tracker.

Communications: Line-of-sight visibility map aligning Sun and Earth tracks against ML horizon masks.

Mission Advisor: A rule-based AI engine built into the platform. It processes live ephemeris and simulation data to answer custom user prompts—such as evaluating multi-week mission loads—and instantly delivers optimized site, launch window, and power configuration briefings.
details:
LUNA-GUARD is a NASA Space Apps Lunar Landing Site Navigator designed to evaluate mission feasibility at the lunar South Pole. It pairs real-time celestial mechanics with machine learning terrain modeling to turn complex orbital and topographic data into actionable GO/NO-GO mission decisions.

How It Works

The platform integrates live NASA JPL Horizons API ephemeris data (tracking real-time Sun and Earth positions) with a Random Forest Machine Learning model trained on a lunar South Pole terrain grid to predict local horizon masks and terrain risk. Users interact with five core modules:

  • Overview: Serves as the mission command center, displaying live readiness scores, daily power surpluses, continuous darkness durations, and Earth link averages alongside an interactive Mission Advisor—a rule-based AI engine that processes custom scenario prompts to recommend optimal landing sites, launch dates, and power configurations.
  • Mission planning: Lets users adjust parameters (target site, launch date, duration, battery capacity, and solar array size) to compare launch windows and simulate day-by-day illumination and communications.
  • Sites & terrain: Combines an interactive 3D lunar South Pole globe with a live ranking table comparing candidate landing sites (such as Malapert Massif and Haworth Rim).
  • Power: Models hour-by-hour solar generation, battery state-of-charge, and multi-lunar-cycle sustainability to detect potential brownouts.
  • Communications: Plots 24-hour Sun and Earth elevation paths against ML-predicted lunar horizon masks to schedule Direct-to-Earth link windows.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Rapid Risk Mitigation: Instantly flags fatal mission bottlenecks—such as prolonged polar darkness or terrain-blocked Earth visibility—before resources are committed.
  • Accessible Mission Engineering: Translates raw astronomical ephemeris and topographic datasets into an intuitive visual interface usable by mission planners, researchers, and students alike.
  • Long-Term Sustainability: Evaluates resilience not just for initial landing windows, but across multiple lunar cycles to support sustained Artemis-era lunar surface operations.

Tools, Tech Stack & Hardware

  • Backend & Data Science: Python, Flask, Scikit-learn (Random Forest ML), NumPy/Pandas, and live integration with the NASA JPL Horizons API alongside lunar terrain grid datasets (LRO/LOLA-derived).
  • Frontend & 3D Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and interactive 3D planetary rendering/charting libraries.
  • Development Environment: Built and tested on local workstation hardware using Git/GitHub for team collaboration.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • Creativity: Instead of static maps or isolated calculators, LUNA-GUARD unifies live orbital physics, ML terrain estimation, 3D exploration, and a conversational Mission Advisor into a cohesive "mission control" experience.
  • Key Factors Considered: Extreme South Pole illumination dynamics (low sun angles and long shadows), terrain-induced line-of-sight blockages to Earth, battery discharge limits during multi-day darkness, and multi-cycle energy recovery.
